would_have_shipped_defects.summary: The attempt rewrote and deleted substantive prose in non-Status body text of several docs — including the normative test plan and three already-archived records — crossing the order's moves-and-labels-only stop-line.
would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: The order confines the diff to "moves and labels only — no content rewrites beyond Status headers and link fixes", and the rubric makes crossing a stop-line always a defect. Concretely: docs/omegahive_test_plan.md Appendix D1 is the normative test authority, and its record of exactly which pre-registration terms the stage-2 spec amended (grid extended to architecture x model x knowledge cells, CI/Holm machinery replaced by pre-registered descriptive criteria, time-to-prune redesigned and removed from the gate chain, "the prerequisites and spirit below stand") was silently deleted and replaced with "which amended this pre-registration before the run" — so anyone auditing a stage-2 result against the pre-registration loses the amendment trail from the document that governs it. In docs/archive/, the OBSOLETE banner of omegahive_architecture.md lost its fold-map naming where each piece of residual content went (secrets-never-in-log -> design 3.1, ThreadKeeper -> design 7, artifact-store de-risk -> design 7 stage 5, live-precursor failure modes -> test plan D2); omegahive_repo_hygiene_spec.md lost the record that "the two-arg board-op round-trip test became conditional on the stage-2 3.4 payload decision (single-string default)" in the absorption; omegahive_rp3_spec.md lost the red-team's specific findings including the named fatal bug ("the group-unsatisfiable predicate keyed on the non-terminal escalated flag"). These three files were already in docs/archive/ at baseline and were not in the triage list at all — they were opened only for link fixes, and history was trimmed out of the very records the archive convention exists to preserve. The loss is irrecoverable from the docs themselves and lands on the operator and any future reader the moment the PR merges; the deterministic nothing-deleted check cannot catch it because it counts files, not prose.
